regions.full_page: God bless you both and all you are interested in. I've had your letter of January 10th here before me on the desk ever since; hoping to get chance and time to send you a worth-while answer. Of course I've been hoping for brighter outlook and better word than what that letter would seem to intimate. Yesterday, however, I received an in- teresting letter from Martha to the effect that all are well in Seat- tle and down the Coast, with one or two exceptions and Helena's Hus- band, E'd Wilhite. From all reports he, your same Edward, has been suffering something similarly to what Father Maurice Joachim went through twenty years ago, when it seemed he was about done for. Yet think how remarkable is his stomach Today. Thanks be to God. I re- ceived a good letter from him last week. Both he and Father Edw'd are well. Thanks be to God and our Bl. Mother Mary. Now I am going to give you briefly something from my "NOTES ON CASES THROUGH THE SERAPHIC MASS ASSOCIATION", that for several years I was making while in Detroit: Just one case in perhaps more than a thousand, -- a number of them not only fearful tumors but of most posi- tive and threatening cancer. May 25th, 1945. "Mrs. Catherine Nagle - 45 - mother of eight children, opened up for operation two weeks ago (May 9th) in Provi- dence Hospital. Found to be so hopelessly full of cancer that the Drs, simply closed her up again as ' ... never to leave the hospital alive.' "Has been enrolled in Ser. Mass Association several times. Today her husband enrolls the Poor Souls specially (10); - whole family storming Heaven by daily Communion .... " Mother comes home To-day; unable to take any nourishment ...
